content: The tobacco industry in Argentina produced a total of 157,294 tonnes of tobacco during the 2003/2004 harvest season. Of this total, the majority, amounting to 93,327 tonnes, was exported. The total area dedicated to tobacco cultivation was 831.75 square kilometers, out of which 776 square kilometers were actually harvested. The industry is predominantly controlled by two major transnational corporations. The first is Massalin Particulares S.A., a subsidiary of Philip Morris, which markets the Marlboro brand and is associated with Tabacos Norte S.A. The second is Nobleza Piccardo, a subsidiary of British American Tobacco, which distributes international brands such as Lucky Strike, Viceroy, and Camel, as well as domestic brands like Jockey and Derby. Tobacco production in Argentina is geographically concentrated in the northern regions of the country. The provinces of Jujuy and Salta, located in the northwest, and Misiones, situated in the northeastern Mesopotamian region, are the leading producers, each contributing over 45,000 tonnes annually. Other provinces involved in tobacco cultivation include Tucumán, Corrientes, Chaco, and Catamarca. Tobacco plays a significant economic role in these regions, which are among the poorer provinces of Argentina. The industry provides employment to approximately 500,000 individuals. Of these, about half are directly engaged in planting and harvesting activities, while only around 2% are involved in the manufacturing of tobacco-derived products. The remaining workforce is employed in distribution and sales. Despite the well-documented health risks associated with smoking, which represent a major public health concern in Argentina, the national government actively supports tobacco producers. This support is provided through the Tobacco Special Fund (Fondo Especial del Tabaco, FET), which offers subsidies and facilitates access to credit.
